frontier.headline: Improved Local Leakage Resilience of Shamir Secret Sharing and Worst-Case Optimal Polynomial Intersection
frontier.summary: We study two problems: Local Leakage Resilience (LLR) for Shamir secret sharing, and worst-case Optimal Polynomial Intersection (OPI). Both problems concern polynomials $Q(X)$ of degree less than $k$, over a prime-order finite field $\mathbb{F}_p$. In LLR for Shamir secret sharing, one asks how much one can learn about $Q(0)$ given a few bits leaked from each of $Q(α_1), \ldots, Q(α_n)$, for distinct non-zero evaluation points $α_i \in \mathbb{F}_p$.

frontier.headline: Constructing Large and Structured Decoherence-Free Subspaces in Hybrid Quantum Systems
frontier.summary: We develop a framework to construct large decoherence-free subspaces with a non-trivial structure. The construction is based on hybrid quantum systems in which quantum matter is coupled to a dissipative bosonic mode. Dissipation imposes a global constraint on the matter by selecting the matter null states in the long-time limit.

frontier.headline: Entanglement entropy and magic of ZX-diagrams
frontier.summary: Entanglement and non-stabilizerness are complementary resources underlying the complexity of quantum states, yet extracting either quantity from large quantum circuits generally requires exponentially scaling resources. In diagrammatic approaches to quantum computation, such as the ZX-calculus, both quantities likewise typically require expensive tensor contractions that are not native to graphical rewriting. Here we show that both entanglement and magic can be efficiently estimated directly from ZX-diagrams.

frontier.headline: Toward Joint Optimization of Circuit Depth and Training Data Size in Adaptively Grown Quantum Classifiers
frontier.summary: Building a quantum model involves a tradeoff: how complex the circuit should be, and how much training data it needs. show that models with fewer trainable gates need less training data to generalize well. Q-FLAIR shows that a quantum feature-map circuit can be grown gate-by-gate, stopping once further growth stops improving the training loss.

frontier.headline: Measure Now, Mitigate Later: Virtual Error Cancellation for Logical Quantum Circuits
frontier.summary: Early fault-tolerant quantum algorithms are a key step in scalable quantum computing, but are ultimately constrained by residual, uncorrectable logical errors. Logical quantum error mitigation can eliminate this bias, however its standard requirements include prior noise characterization, more complex experiments, and substantial sampling overhead. Although no mitigation technique can simultaneously overcome all three constraints, we demonstrate that the first two---noise learning and need for modified circuits---can be completely bypassed for logical circuits by leveraging only syndrome records.

voices.headline: The GOP’s Message to Immigrants
voices.summary: Only a few decades ago, Republican presidents would happily evoke the idea of America as a haven for people around the world. Ronald Reagan, in his farewell speech, declared that “anyone, from any corner of the Earth, can come to live in America and become an American.” Reagan was no paragon of racial tolerance—he opposed the civil-rights movement and privately referred to Black people as “ monkeys ”—but he did not regard the presence of nonwhite people as an existential threat to America. For years the Republican Party insisted that what it wanted was a certain kind of immigrant—highly skilled people who came here legally, or even, not that long ago, those brought to the U.S.

voices.headline: Three Years After October 7, I Moved Back to Nahal Oz
voices.summary: O n the morning of August 18 , shortly after 10 a.m., a moving truck stopped in front of our home in Kibbutz Nahal Oz, the closest Israeli community to the Gaza border. The driver and two assistants began unloading dozens of boxes containing our belongings—books, clothing, electronics, kitchen appliances. Fifty minutes later, everything was off the truck, the boxes piled in the center of our living room.

voices.headline: If You Want a Real Digital Commons, Build It Yourself
voices.summary: For more than a decade, the Philippines has been a test case for how technology enables an authoritarian state to capture and corrode the institutions that make democracy work. The work of Rodrigo Duterte, the autocratic president of the Philippines from 2016 to 2022, would hardly have been possible without that of Mark Zuckerberg, the CEO of what was then the most powerful social-media company. The Philippine state used Facebook to turn bottom-up social-media attacks into lawfare.

voices.headline: Public Execution Won’t Have the Effect Trump Intends
voices.summary: Before the mid-19th century, executions in America were presumptively public. Most prisoners were hanged on a gallows, following an hours-long affair that began with the condemned person’s exit from jail accompanied by ministers, the sheriff and his deputies, and sometimes a military escort. Spectators joined the humiliating procession, gathering by the thousands to watch the noose lowered over the prisoner’s neck.
